summary: NVMe namespace ID rename during controller firmware update breaks SCCM task sequence on imaging stations
description:
Issue summary: Multiple depot imaging stations intermittently fail the SCCM task sequence during OS apply when the primary NVMe device is re-enumerated with a new Namespace ID (NSUID) after recent controller firmware updates applied in depot repairs. The TS aborts with errors about missing OS partition path and cannot locate the image. This started after a coordinated firmware roll applied to a batch of replacement NVMe drives used in depot replacements.

Expected behaviour: SCCM task sequence should detect the correct disk identifier and proceed with partitioning and OS apply regardless of controller-level namespace ID changes.

Observed behaviour: On affected machines the TS aborts mid-way with errors referencing the original disk GUID/identifier (e.g., \?\IDE#Ven_*#Disk&Ven_*), and SMSTSLog shows the target partition/path does not exist because the OS disk device node moved (NVMe namespace rename).
impact: ~8 imaging stations impacted across two depots. ~120 devices attempted imaging in the last 48 hours; ~22 devices failed and required manual intervention. Delays to standard depot turnaround (RMA reimage SLA) and downstream device shipping delays. Internal incident escalated because this blocks automated provisioning for replacement devices.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start an SCCM task sequence on a test station with an NVMe drive that has had controller firmware updated to the vendor's version that renames namespaces.
2) Allow the machine to reboot during the Apply OS step where the TS expects the disk to be at a specific device path.
3) Observe SMSTS.log during the 'Format and Partition Disk' step: the expected disk node is no longer present and a new NVMe namespace ID is enumerated.
4) Task sequence fails with error 0x80070002 (file not found) referring to a path on the previously enumerated device GUID.
logs: SMSTS.log excerpt 2026-03-01 09:12:45: Attempting to access \\?\IDE#Disk&Ven_ABC...\n  Device not found.
Kernel: nvme 0000:01:00.0: namespace id changed: nsid 1 -> nsid 3
Previously recorded Disk0 at start of TS had nsid:1
investigation_notes: 03-01 10:00 Priya: Reproduced failure on Dell Precision 5570 with vendor FW v2.11 -> v2.12 applied. NVMe controller firmware release notes mention namespace reassignments when migrating namespaces between controllers for wear leveling changes.
03-01 11:20 SRE: WinPE enumerates NVMe devices by namespace ID; SCCM TS uses device path recorded earlier in the TS environment which becomes stale after NSUID changes.
03-01 14:00 Eng: Confirmed this only occurs when firmware reassigns NSUID on first boot after replacement; drives that already had updated FW in inventory did not trigger the problem.

Hypothesis: Depot firmware script applies FW in pre-provision step which causes NVMe controller to rewrite namespace metadata; SCCM TS template expects stable device GUIDs and doesn't resolve new namespace mapping in WinPE stage.
Temporary mitigation test: Modified TS to reference disk by disk index (DiskNumber) instead of persistent device GUID to avoid namespace mismatch; test images succeed in WinPE when disk index used.
Risks: Disk index can change with multiple storage devices; need robust detection (e.g., enumerate NVMe model+serial in WinPE and map to disk).
comments: 03-01 15:04 Jordan Kim (Reporter): Logged initial findings and opened this ticket after depot team reported spike in reimage failures.
03-01 16:12 Depot Lead - Miguel Alvarez: Confirmed 14/16 failures correspond to drives with new FW v2.12 from vendor batch 'Q1-RMA-2026'. Providing batch serial list to Eng.
03-02 09:30 Priya Singh (Assignee): Implemented PoC TS change to detect NVMe by serial number in WinPE using wmic and map to DiskNumber. PoC passes for 5 repro cases. Planning to push to staging TS.
03-02 13:20 SRE - Anya Petrova: Noted this will require coordination with vendor to avoid future namespace reassignments in depot flow. Opened vendor support case (INC-2026-0893).

03-03 10:05 Priya Singh: Created temp runbook for depot techs to avoid applying FW in depot prior to imaging unless necessary; provided manual recovery steps for stuck devices (boot into WinPE, run diskpart, rescan, map by serial).
resolution: Workaround (applied 2026-03-02): Update SCCM task sequence in staging to map NVMe devices by model+serial in WinPE and derive DiskNumber at runtime. Deployed to two depot staging stations; verified success on 12 test images.

Short-term remediation: Added pre-provision validation step to depot firmware scripts to skip namespace-reassigning FW on devices destined for immediate imaging. Depot ops notified via runbook update.

Long-term fix: Eng to coordinate with NVMe vendor to obtain firmware revision that preserves namespace IDs or provides stable mapping on first boot. Also plan TS refactor to rely on NVMe serial/model matching rather than persistent device GUIDs in WinPE.

Follow-ups: Create automated check in depot intake to detect drives with FW versions known to reassign namespaces (action item assigned to Eng - due 2026-03-18). Update Confluence imaging runbook with recovery steps and vendor ticket link.
Status: mitigation in place, Eng working with vendor. Ticket remains In Progress until vendor provides FW guidance and TS refactor completed.
